questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: A chant and its unaccompanied unison
questions.stem: During handover, a nurse describes a chant sung in unison without accompaniment; which texture is this?

options.text: A monophonic texture of one unison melodic line
A polyphonic texture with several overlapping voices
A homophonic texture with melody and accompaniment
A heterophonic texture with varied simultaneous lines
options.misconception: mistakes unison for varied parallel lines

questions.explanation: An unaccompanied unison chant has one melodic line, so it is monophonic; polyphonic and homophonic textures need multiple independent or supporting lines.
questions.hint: Count the independent melodic lines present.

questions.topic: Doubling a pitch standard up two octaves
questions.learningObjective: Compute a frequency raised two octaves
questions.stem: A nurse notes a tuning fork at 440 Hz; what frequency results from raising it two octaves?

options.text: 880 Hz, the pitch raised by one octave only
options.misconception: stops after a single octave doubling

options.text: 1760 Hz, the pitch raised by two octaves
3520 Hz, the pitch raised by four octaves

questions.explanation: Raising 440 Hz by two octaves multiplies by four, giving 1760 Hz; one octave would be 880 Hz.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: Telling a monophonic texture from a polyphonic one
questions.stem: In handover, a nurse asks how to tell monophonic from polyphonic texture; write a short explanation.

answer.exemplar: Monophonic texture presents a single melodic line with no accompaniment, whereas polyphonic texture combines two or more independent melodic lines sounding together.

questions.explanation: The distinction rests on the number of independent lines; monophony has one, polyphony has several, and homophony keeps a main melody with support.
